Null-split calibration check of normalization and model

Source: R/tidyMS_null_split.R
null_split_check.Rd

Splits the samples within every stratum at random into two pseudo-groups, A and B, and tests B against A with build_contrast_analysis(). No feature differs between the pseudo-groups, so a calibrated pipeline gives uniform p-values: about 5% below 0.05, 1% below 0.01, and no feature with FDR < 0.05. The check uses no labels beyond the strata, so it compares normalizations without favouring any of them by construction.

Usage

null_split_check(
  lfqdata,
  method = "lm",
  n_splits = 20,
  strata = lfqdata$relevant_factor_keys(),
  n_features = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

lfqdata

the model input: a normalized LFQData object, aggregated or not as method requires.

method

facade name passed to build_contrast_analysis().

n_splits

one positive whole number of distinct random splits.

strata

factor keys within whose levels the samples are split; the model is ~ <strata> + pseudo_group_. character(0) splits all samples as one group; subset lfqdata to one condition first.

n_features

NULL (default) tests all top-level features (hierarchy_keys()[1]); one positive whole number tests that many, chosen at random.

seed

NULL (default) uses the current random number generator state; one whole number runs the draws under withr::with_seed().

...

further arguments to build_contrast_analysis().

Value

A tibble with one row per split: split, n (tests with a p-value), p_below_0.05, p_below_0.01 (shares of p-values), n_FDR_below_0.05, ks_D (Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance of the p-values from the uniform distribution), and the list-columns assignment (sample name and pseudo_group_ per sample) and contrasts (subject keys, diff, p.value and FDR).

Details

Within each stratum the samples are split into halves; an odd number of samples gives halves that differ by one. Splits that differ only by swapping A and B count as one. When the design has fewer distinct splits than n_splits, all of them are returned with a message.

Read the median and range over splits. Splits share samples, so they are not independent replicates. A split that follows a batch or the run order puts a real technical effect into the contrast: compare assignment with the batch of each sample, and persistent hits point to a batch effect the normalization left in. With few samples per pseudo-group, variance moderation and imputation behave differently than in the real comparison; calibration carries over, power does not.

See also

build_contrast_analysis()

Other stats: INTERNAL_FUNCTIONS_BY_FAMILY, fdr_sig_level(), pooled_variance_explained(), power_fdr_prior_n(), summarize_variance_explained()

Examples

bb <- sim_lfq_data_protein_config(n_proteins = 50, with_missing = FALSE)
#> `protein_Id`: columns `proteinID`, `idtype2` united with separator '~'.
#> creating sampleName from file_name column
#> setup_analysis: dropped 5 unconfigured columns: average_prot_abundance, sd, mean, N, Replicate.
lfqdata <- LFQData$new(bb$data, bb$config)
lfqdata$is_transformed(TRUE)
res <- null_split_check(lfqdata, method = "limma", n_splits = 5, seed = 1)
res[, c("split", "n", "p_below_0.05", "n_FDR_below_0.05", "ks_D")]
#> # A tibble: 5 × 5
#>   split     n p_below_0.05 n_FDR_below_0.05   ks_D
#>   <int> <int>        <dbl>            <int>  <dbl>
#> 1     1    50         0.08                0 0.154 
#> 2     2    50         0.04                0 0.132 
#> 3     3    50         0.06                0 0.107 
#> 4     4    50         0.04                0 0.0632
#> 5     5    50         0.02                0 0.0614
